intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Native BNB leaves the wallet on BNB Chain. Native AVAX is what can arrive on Avalanche C-Chain. The coin that pays gas changes with the network.

Both sides quote 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, a label for the native coin rather than a contract with code. Chain id 56 confirms in about 3 seconds on BscScan. Chain id 43114 is the C-Chain, and the credit belongs on Snowtrace. The X-Chain stays empty. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers why these two balances never merge.
description: Native BNB leaves BNB Chain, chain id 56, and native AVAX arrives on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Match the debit on BscScan and the credit on Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Fee and principal share one BNB balance
sections.body: The network fee and the amount you sell both come out of BNB. Sending every last unit leaves chain 56 unpaid. Keep a remainder. This quote never spends WBNB at 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c.

sections.heading: WAVAX is a different receive
sections.body: Native AVAX can pay later C-Chain fees. The wrapped token at 0xB31f66AA3C1e785363F0875A1B74E27b85FD66c7 will not appear from this quote. If a pool asked for WAVAX, this output is the wrong one.

sections.heading: Two explorers, two coins
sections.body: BscScan records BNB leaving chain 56. Snowtrace records AVAX on the C-Chain only. The placeholder text matches and the assets do not. Match the signing wallet and the full address, not a shortened prefix.

sections.heading: Price can move before you sign
sections.body: BNB against AVAX can reprice while the quote sits open. Take the minimum shown or request a fresh quote. No finish time is stated for the bridge leg. A dollar output on Avalanche is a different route.

faqs.question: Why is the address the same on both chains?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE marks native gas, and each chain defines its own. On BNB Chain, chain id 56, it is BNB. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, it is AVAX. There is no approval for that label. BscScan shows the debit and Snowtrace shows the C-Chain credit.

faqs.question: I hold WBNB. Will this quote spend it?
faqs.answer: No. WBNB is the BEP-20 at 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. This page spends native BNB only. If the balance you mean is WBNB, you are on the wrong route. Unwrap on BNB Chain or open a quote that names the WBNB contract. BscScan will show that contract, not a native debit.

faqs.question: Must I already hold AVAX to receive it?
faqs.answer: You need BNB on chain 56 for the sale and for gas. A prior AVAX balance is not required for the credit to be created. The receive address must be a C-Chain address. X-Chain AVAX is a different system and will not show this credit.

intro:
Swap USDC from BNB Chain to USDT on Solana. Circle USDC leaves BNB Chain. Tether USDT is what can arrive on Solana. The issuer changes, and so does the wallet that can hold the result.

Spend 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Circle USDC on BNB Chain with 18 decimals. Receive the SPL mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, Tether USDT with 6 decimals. Chain id 56 still needs BNB for gas, and BscScan shows that debit. Solana has no chain id and no ERC-20 approval. Phantom and Solscan are the receive side. A 0x address cannot hold the mint. Steps live in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains).
description: Circle USDC leaves BNB Chain at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Tether USDT arrives on Solana. Check BscScan, then the mint on Solscan in Phantom.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals become six
sections.body: A raw unit on BNB Chain USDC is not a raw unit of Solana USDT. The quote already converts them. If you compare the integer in the wallet data to the decimal amount, you will invent a loss that is only a decimals gap. Read the human amount on the quote.

sections.heading: This is Tether, not Circle, on the far side
sections.body: Keeping the USDC ticker would mean the Solana mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. This route does not pay that mint. If your books need Circle USDC on Solana, you are on the wrong page.

sections.heading: The Solana side never asks for an approval
sections.body: BNB Chain may ask you to approve 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d before the swap. Solana will not. Phantom signs a different kind of transaction. MetaMask on chain 56 cannot display the USDT that arrives.

sections.heading: Empty Phantom wallets cannot pay later fees
sections.body: USDT on Solana is not gas. A Phantom account with zero SOL can receive the mint and still be unable to move it. This route does not deliver SOL. Get a little SOL first if the destination wallet is new.

faqs.question: Is BNB Chain USDC the same contract as Ethereum USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and uses 6 decimals. This route spends 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on chain id 56, which uses 18 decimals. If the wallet is on Ethereum, the quote is wrong. Confirm the chain before you approve. BscScan should show the 18 decimal contract. Match it before you sign.

faqs.question: Why would I check Solscan if I signed on BscScan?
faqs.answer: BscScan only sees the Circle USDC debit and the BNB gas on chain 56. The Tether mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is an SPL account. Solscan is where that credit can show. The two explorers never list one shared balance. Open Phantom and search that mint, not the ticker alone.

faqs.question: Can I paste my MetaMask address as the receiver?
faqs.answer: No. Solana receivers are base58 public keys, not 0x strings. A MetaMask address will not hold Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Use Phantom or another Solana wallet. There is no ERC-20 approval on that side to fall back on. Solscan will not credit an EVM deposit address. Paste a Phantom address only.

intro:
Swap USDC from BNB Chain to SOL on Solana. Circle USDC leaves BNB Chain. SOL is what can arrive on Solana. You sell a dollar token and take price exposure in the destination gas coin.

The token you approve on chain 56 is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Circle USDC with 18 decimals. The output mint is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, the wrapped SOL mint routes use when they quote SOL. It is not an ERC-20. BscScan shows the USDC debit. Solscan shows the SOL side. Network notes for the source sit on [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc).
description: Circle USDC on BNB Chain is sold for SOL on Solana. Spend 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d and confirm the SOL mint on Solscan. Phantom holds the SOL.

sections.heading: The peg stops at the moment you sign
sections.body: USDC is Circle's dollar token. SOL is not. The amount of SOL you accept is the minimum on the quote, and that figure can look worse a minute later if you wait and the quote expires. Request a new quote rather than forcing the old one.

sections.heading: So111 is how routes name SOL
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the wrapped SOL mint, not a BEP-20 and not native BNB. People looking for an ERC-20 called SOL on BNB Chain are on the wrong asset. Phantom shows SOL. MetaMask on chain 56 will not.

sections.heading: Approval stays on BNB Chain
sections.body: You may approve 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, then sign the swap, and both of those transactions burn BNB. Solana has no ERC-20 approval for the mint that arrives. Leave BNB on chain 56 so the second signature can pay gas.

sections.heading: A stablecoin destination is a different quote
sections.body: If the job was Tether USDT at Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, or Circle USDC on Solana, this page is wrong. Those mints do not pay Solana fees either. This one pays you SOL, which can.

faqs.question: Does So111 mean I receive a wrapped token I cannot spend as SOL?
faqs.answer: Routes quote SOL with the mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. In Phantom that balance is the SOL you use for fees and swaps. It is not an ERC-20 on BNB Chain, and it is not WETH. Confirm the mint on Solscan before you treat a lookalike ticker as SOL.

faqs.question: What if I wanted to keep USDC?
faqs.answer: Then do not use this pair. The source 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d is sold. Nothing on Solana remains Circle USDC from this quote. Pick a route whose output mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v if the dollar token has to stay Circle. This page pays SOL on purpose. Do not stay here if you need dollars.

faqs.question: Which explorer shows the SOL?
faqs.answer: BscScan shows the USDC leaving chain id 56 and the BNB spent on gas, about a 3 second block. Solscan shows the destination mint. There is no Solana chain id to select in an EVM wallet. The bridge leg itself has no fixed finish time on this page.

Swap USDT from BNB Chain to USDC on Solana. Tether USDT leaves BNB Chain. Circle USDC is what can arrive on Solana. Same rough peg, different company, different account model.

description: Tether USDT leaves BNB Chain and Circle USDC arrives on Solana. Match 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan and the SPL mint on Solscan.

sections.heading: Do not expect the USDT mint to show up
sections.body: Staying in Tether on Solana would mean Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. This quote buys Circle instead. If a treasury rule says the destination must remain USDT, this route is the wrong one even though both tokens aim at one dollar.

sections.heading: The integer in the logs will not match
sections.body: BNB Chain USDT uses 18 decimals. Solana USDC uses 6. The quote speaks in human units. Judging the fill by the raw on-chain integer makes a 12-zero gap look like a missing balance. Read the decimal amount, then the mint on Solscan.

sections.heading: Gas is BNB, then later a little SOL
sections.body: Chain id 56 takes BNB for the approval of 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 and for the swap. The USDC you receive cannot pay Solana fees. A brand new Phantom with no SOL can hold the mint and still be stuck until SOL is added.

sections.heading: No approval exists on the mint side
sections.body: Solana will not ask you to approve EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v the way an ERC-20 does. If a site on the destination asks for an unlimited allowance in MetaMask, you are not looking at this route anymore.

faqs.question: Is this the Ethereum Tether contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum USDT is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and it uses 6 decimals. This page spends 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain id 56, an 18 decimal Tether. Approving the Ethereum contract will not fund the Solana USDC mint. Check the network badge first. BscScan lists this 18 decimal contract. Match it on chain 56.

faqs.question: Where do I see the Circle credit?
faqs.answer: BscScan shows Tether leaving and BNB gas on chain 56, where blocks are about 3 seconds. Solscan shows EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Those pages do not share a transaction list. The bridge leg has no published finish time here. Open the Circle mint once Phantom shows the account.

faqs.question: Can the receiver be an exchange EVM deposit address?
faqs.answer: Only if that venue gave you a Solana deposit address for USDC, which will not start with 0x. An ERC-20 deposit address on BNB Chain will not receive this SPL mint. Confirm the asset and the network on the deposit screen before you paste. The venue must say Solana.

You spend 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, Tether on chain id 56, 18 decimals. You are quoted against So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, the wrapped SOL mint. description: Tether USDT on BNB Chain converts to SOL on Solana. Spend 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 and confirm the mint on Solscan. Phantom is the receiver.

sections.heading: You are leaving the peg on purpose
sections.body: USDT is Tether's token. SOL moves with its own market. If the point of the transfer was a dollar balance you can spend later without price risk, this route is wrong. Stop and choose a USDC or USDT mint on Solana.

sections.heading: Wrapped SOL mint, not a BEP-20
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is how Solana routes name SOL. It is not WETH, and it is not a contract you approve on BscScan. Phantom is where the spendable SOL balance belongs.

sections.heading: Two signatures may spend BNB
sections.body: Approving 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is its own transaction. The swap is another. Both need BNB on chain 56. Solana does not add an ERC-20 approval after that. Keep BNB back so the second signature is possible.

sections.heading: Ethereum Tether will not fund this
sections.body: The contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 lives on Ethereum, chain id 1. This page never sees it. If the wallet network is Ethereum or Polygon, you are about to approve the wrong chain.

faqs.question: Will the SOL show up inside MetaMask?
faqs.answer: No. MetaMask on chain 56 can show the Tether debit at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. The SOL credit is an SPL balance around So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Open Phantom and Solscan. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana to watch for. A 0x receiver never displays that mint. Use the address Phantom shows you.

faqs.question: What if the quote expires while I compare prices?
faqs.answer: Let it expire. USDT against SOL can move while you read. A fresh quote gives a new minimum. This page does not publish a finish time for the bridge leg. BNB Chain blocks near 3 seconds only describe the source chain, not the full route.

faqs.question: Is BNB Chain USDT 6 decimals like Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 uses 18 decimals. Ethereum's Tether uses 6. Solana SOL is not a 6 decimal stable either. Compare the amount written on the quote, not the raw integer in a log line on BscScan. The two contracts are not substitutes. Human units on the quote are the ones that count.

Swap ETH from BNB Chain to USDC on Solana. The BNB Chain ETH token leaves that chain. Circle USDC is what can arrive on Solana. You are not moving native ether off Ethereum.

The source token is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, Binance-Peg ETH, an 18 decimal BEP-20. It is not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and it does not pay gas. Gas is BNB on chain id 56. The output mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. BscScan, then Solscan. More on the source network is on [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc).
description: Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain converts to Circle USDC on Solana. The source token is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Confirm it on BscScan.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH is not the gas coin
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 cannot pay BNB Chain fees. You still need BNB. If the balance you meant was native BNB at 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, this route is wrong. Native gas and pegged ETH are different lines in the wallet.

sections.heading: Mainnet ether is on chain id 1
sections.body: Ethereum ETH and Ethereum WETH live on chain id 1, with about 12 second blocks, and Etherscan is their explorer. This quote never touches them. A wallet left on Ethereum will try to spend a token this route does not use.

sections.heading: Arrival is Circle USDC, not ether
sections.body: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is Circle's SPL USDC. It will not pay Solana fees by itself. If you needed SOL, or Tether's mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, choose that output instead.

sections.heading: Phantom is the only sensible receiver
sections.body: Solana has no ERC-20 approval and no EVM chain id. Paste a Phantom address. Solscan is where the USDC mint should be checked. BscScan will only show the pegged ETH debit and the BNB fee.

faqs.question: Is this token WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The token this route sells is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain. ETH is not WETH, and pegged ETH is a third asset. Approving the Ethereum WETH contract does nothing for this quote. Gas on chain 56 is still BNB. Keep some BNB aside.

faqs.question: Will USDC on Solana pay my Phantom fees?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC at EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is not SOL. Keep a little SOL in Phantom if you need to move the USDC after it arrives. This route does not add that SOL for you. Solscan shows the mint, not a gas credit. Fund that SOL separately.

faqs.question: What do I look up on BscScan?
faqs.answer: The debit of 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and the BNB fee on chain id 56. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. That timing is not the bridge finish. The Circle mint is only visible on Solscan, from a Solana address. It never appears on BscScan. Phantom is where that mint can show.

sections.heading: Three different things called ETH

sections.heading: BNB pays, the pegged token does not
sections.body: Chain id 56 fees come from BNB, and blocks are about 3 seconds. You may approve 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 first. That approval is not the swap. Solana will not ask for a second ERC-20 approval.

sections.body: After arrival you hold Tether, not SOL. A Phantom wallet with no SOL can receive Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB and still fail the next transfer. Fund a little SOL before you need to move it.

faqs.question: Does BscScan call this token Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The contract 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is Binance-Peg ETH on chain id 56. The name can say Ethereum and still not be native ETH or WETH. Read the contract, not the ticker. Native BNB is the only gas coin on that chain. Etherscan is the wrong explorer for this debit.

faqs.question: Which mint should Solscan show?
faqs.answer: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. If the account shows EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, that is Circle USDC and not this route.
