sections.body: If the destination must be Tether, the mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB and this route is wrong. Circle and Tether are different issuers even when both say one dollar. Pick the mint your books named.

sections.heading: The USDC cannot pay Phantom
sections.body: Receiving Circle USDC does not give you SOL. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the SOL mint, and this quote does not buy it. A new Phantom wallet needs SOL from somewhere else before it can move the USDC.

faqs.question: Is 0xEeee a contract I should approve?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the native gas label. On chain id 56 it means BNB. There is no bytecode to approve. If a wallet asks you to approve that string as an ERC-20, you are not on this route. BscScan shows a native BNB transfer, not a token approval.

faqs.question: Does the USDC arrive inside the same MetaMask account?
faqs.answer: Only the debit does. MetaMask can show BNB leaving on chain 56. The Circle mint EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is SPL. Open Phantom and Solscan. Solana has no chain id and no ERC-20 approval. A 0x receiver will not hold it. Search the mint, not the word USDC.

faqs.question: What if I wanted BNB to become SOL?
faqs.answer: This page pays USDC, not SOL. You give up BNB price exposure and take Circle's dollar token. A quote aimed at So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the SOL route. Using this one and hoping for gas on Solana will leave you short. Read the output before you sign.

intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to USDT on Solana. Native BNB leaves BNB Chain. Tether USDT is what can arrive on Solana. The gas coin on chain 56 becomes a Tether mint that does not pay fees in Phantom.

Spend the native label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Receive Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. WBNB is not involved. BscScan is the source explorer, blocks about 3 seconds. Solscan is the destination explorer. No ERC-20 approval runs on Solana. The source chain notes are on [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc).
description: Native BNB on chain id 56 converts to Tether USDT on Solana. The gas label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Then check Solscan in Phantom.

sections.heading: Native BNB, not the wrapped contract
sections.body: 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c is WBNB. This quote ignores it. If your wallet holds WBNB and almost no native BNB, you cannot pay gas and you are on the wrong asset. Unwrap first or change the quote.

sections.heading: Tether's mint is the whole point
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is Tether, 6 decimals. Circle's Solana USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. If you told an exchange you would deposit Circle USDC, this route is wrong.

sections.heading: Keep BNB for the fee
sections.body: The amount you bridge and the chain 56 fee share one balance. Drain it and the signature fails before Solscan has anything to show. There is no separate gas token hiding behind the 0xEeee label.

sections.heading: USDT sits still without SOL
sections.body: Tether on Solana cannot pay the next Phantom fee. This route does not include SOL. If the destination wallet is empty of SOL, the USDT can arrive and wait. That is a gas problem, not a missing mint.

faqs.question: Will BscScan show a token approval for BNB?
faqs.answer: It should show a native BNB debit on chain id 56, not an approval of 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That string is a gas label, not a contract. If you are approving WBNB instead, you picked a different token than this page sells. Native transfers do not sit in the token approval tab.

faqs.question: How do I confirm Tether and not Circle?
faqs.answer: Solscan should list Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. The Circle mint is a different string. Phantom is the wallet that can hold it. There is no ERC-20 approval on that side, and a 0x address is not a Solana receiver. Search the full mint, not the ticker. Look on Solscan after Phantom updates.

faqs.question: Does a 3 second block mean the USDT is already there?
faqs.answer: No. About 3 seconds is the BNB Chain block, visible on BscScan. It is not a finish time for the bridge. Solscan shows the mint only after the destination leg. If the quote expired, request a new minimum before you sign again. A fast source block is not the whole route.

intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to SOL on Solana. Native BNB leaves BNB Chain. SOL is what can arrive on Solana. You trade one network's gas coin for the other's, across two account models.

BNB is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. SOL is quoted as So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Those strings are not the same kind of address. BscScan shows the BNB debit. Solscan shows SOL. Blocks on the source are about 3 seconds. Solana has no ERC-20 approval. Read [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) if a single seed phrase made the two balances look interchangeable.
description: Native BNB leaves BNB Chain and SOL arrives on Solana. The gas label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Confirm SOL on Solscan in Phantom.

sections.heading: Leave a BNB remainder on chain 56
sections.body: You are spending the fee coin. The last BNB cannot pay for its own departure. WBNB at 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c is the wrong balance entirely. This quote wants native BNB only.

sections.heading: So111 is the route's name for SOL
sections.body: Phantom spends that balance as SOL. It is not an ERC-20, not WETH, and not WBTC. WBTC is not native bitcoin, and this hop does not involve bitcoin at all. Solscan is the check. MetaMask will not list the credit.

sections.heading: Both prices move
sections.body: BNB and SOL are volatile against each other. The minimum on the quote is the deal. Refresh it if you pause. Nothing here dates the bridge leg. A 3 second BscScan block only means the source chain moved.

sections.heading: Dollar mints are other jobs
sections.body: Circle USDC on Solana is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Tether is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. If you needed either peg, this SOL route is wrong. You would also need SOL already if you wanted to move those mints later.

faqs.question: Are the two gas labels the same address type?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is an EVM stand-in for BNB on chain id 56. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is a Solana mint for SOL. You do not approve either one as an ERC-20 on the destination. BscScan and Solscan are separate records. Do not approve the SOL mint on BscScan.

faqs.question: Can I receive SOL in the wallet that holds the BNB?
faqs.answer: Only if that wallet also has a Solana address, such as Phantom, and you pasted that address. The 0x account on chain 56 is not a Solana receiver. There is no ERC-20 approval step that fixes a wrong address type. Paste the address Phantom shows, then check Solscan.

faqs.question: What if the wallet holds WBNB instead of BNB?
faqs.answer: Then this route cannot spend it. WBNB is 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. Native BNB is the gas label. Unwrap, or request a quote that names WBNB. You still must keep native BNB for the chain 56 fee. A wallet of only WBNB cannot pay gas. Unwrap to native BNB before you return.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to USDT on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. Tether USDT is what can arrive on Ethereum. The issuer changes, and the gas coin on the far side is ETH.

Sell 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, native Circle USDC on chain id 137. That is not USDC.e. Buy 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, Tether on chain id 1. Polygon blocks are about 2 seconds. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. Polygonscan shows the debit. Etherscan shows the credit. POL pays the source fee. Network notes are on [Polygon](/chains/polygon).
description: Circle USDC leaves Polygon and Tether USDT arrives on Ethereum. Spend 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Confirm the credit on Etherscan, chain id 1.

sections.heading: Native USDC is not the bridged copy
sections.body: USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is the older bridged dollar on Polygon. This quote spends 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. If the wallet shows USDC.e, you are on the wrong token. Polygonscan will show which contract the approval used.

sections.heading: Tether on Ethereum is not gas
sections.body: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 cannot pay Ethereum fees. You need ETH already on chain id 1 or the USDT sits still. This route does not deliver that ETH. A route that quotes native ETH is a different job.

sections.heading: Circle in, Tether out
sections.body: Staying with Circle would mean Ethereum USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This page buys Tether instead. If a venue told you to deposit Circle USDC on Ethereum, this route is wrong even though both tokens target one dollar.

sections.heading: POL on the way out
sections.body: Chain id 137 charges POL, the native coin, not USDC. The label for that gas is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and this quote does not sell it. Leave POL in the wallet. An approval of USDC plus the swap can be two transactions.

faqs.question: I hold USDC.e. Is this the right contract?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route spends native Circle USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on chain id 137. Polygonscan shows the contract you approved. If the balance is the bridged copy, switch tokens before you sign. Native USDC and USDC.e are not one balance. Check Polygonscan before the allowance.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay my Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not ETH. Chain id 1 charges ETH, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. That block time is not a finish time for the bridge. Keep ETH on Ethereum or the new USDT cannot move. About 12 second blocks are not a bridge finish time.

faqs.question: Where do I look up each side?
faqs.answer: Polygonscan shows the Circle debit on chain id 137. Etherscan shows Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. The pages do not share a balance. If you wanted Circle USDC on Ethereum instead, the contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and this route is wrong. Tether is a different issuer. Do not deposit it where Circle was requested.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to DAI on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. You are switching issuers, not moving one dollar token under a new name.

The sale is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on chain id 137. The purchase is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F, Maker DAO's DAI on chain id 1. Polygonscan records the USDC. Etherscan records the DAI. POL pays gas on Polygon. ETH pays gas after arrival. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that DAI can be checked.
description: Circle USDC on Polygon converts to Maker DAI on Ethereum. Source 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Read the DAI credit on Etherscan. DAI is not USDC.

sections.heading: DAI is Maker, not Circle and not Tether
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is Maker's stablecoin. It can trade away from one dollar. If you needed Ethereum USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 or Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, this route is the wrong output.

sections.heading: USDC.e will not fill the order
sections.body: The older bridged dollar on Polygon is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This page wants native Circle USDC. Approving USDC.e spends a token the quote did not name. Check the approval target on Polygonscan.

sections.heading: DAI cannot pay mainnet fees
sections.body: After the credit you still need ETH on chain id 1. DAI is not gas, and ETH is not WETH. The native gas label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on Ethereum means ETH. This quote does not buy that label.

sections.heading: Leave POL behind on chain 137
sections.body: Polygon fees come from POL. Blocks there are about 2 seconds, which only describes the source chain. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. Neither number is a bridge finish time. If the quote expires, request a new minimum.

faqs.question: Is DAI the same organization as USDC?
faqs.answer: No. USDC is issued by Circle. DAI is Maker's token at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. This route sells Circle on Polygon and buys Maker on Ethereum. If your books must stay in Circle, use a USDC output. Etherscan is where the DAI contract is confirmed. A shared dollar target is not a shared issuer.

faqs.question: What if my Polygon balance says USDC but the swap will not quote?
faqs.answer: You may be holding USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 rather than 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. This page is wrong for the bridged copy. Polygonscan lists both. Chain id 137 and a POL balance are still required for gas. Approve only the native contract. The ticker USDC on its own is not enough.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH before DAI arrives?
faqs.answer: You need POL on Polygon to send, and you need ETH on Ethereum if you want to move the DAI afterward. DAI itself will not pay chain id 1. The route does not include that ETH. About 12 second Ethereum blocks are not the bridge clock.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to ETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. Native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. You sell a dollar token and receive the coin that pays gas on chain id 1.

Spend 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Receive the native gas label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which on Ethereum means ETH, not WETH. Polygonscan shows the USDC debit. Etherscan shows ETH, not a token transfer to WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. See [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) before you treat this as a same-chain wrap.
description: Circle USDC leaves Polygon and native ETH arrives on Ethereum. The ETH label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Confirm it on Etherscan, not WETH.

sections.heading: This ETH can pay fees
sections.body: On chain id 1 the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is spendable ETH. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 cannot pay gas until you unwrap it. If a contract asked for WETH, this route is the wrong output.

sections.heading: USDC.e is a different Polygon balance
sections.body: Native Circle USDC is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. Holding only the bridged token means this quote cannot spend your dollars. Match the contract on Polygonscan.

sections.heading: POL stays on Polygon
sections.body: You pay POL for chain id 137, about a 2 second block. That POL does not become the ETH you receive. Leave enough POL for the approval and the swap. Draining POL and hoping USDC covers gas will fail the send.

sections.heading: The dollar peg ends when you sign
sections.body: ETH moves against USDC while a quote is open. Accept the minimum or refresh it. Ethereum blocks near 12 seconds are the destination chain, not a promise about the bridge. Etherscan is where the ETH credit belongs.

faqs.question: Is the destination WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route pays native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. ETH is not WETH. Etherscan should show a native credit, not a WETH token transfer. If you needed the wrapper, pick the WETH route. Native ETH and WETH are different lines in the wallet.

faqs.question: Can I start from USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. The quote names 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Polygonscan will show an approval of the wrong contract if you force the bridged token. Switch to native USDC first. Chain id 137 must be selected. Holding only USDC.e means this quote cannot see your dollars.

faqs.question: Does Polygon POL show up as ETH?
faqs.answer: No. POL is the gas coin on chain id 137. ETH is the gas coin on chain id 1. They share no balance. The 0xEeee label means whichever native coin the chain uses. Etherscan and Polygonscan are separate records. POL never arrives as ETH on chain id 1.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to WETH on Ethereum. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. WETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. The wrapper is not gas, so a wallet with only that WETH still cannot pay chain id 1.

You sell 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and buy 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH would have been the label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. This page does not buy that label. Polygonscan shows the USDC. Etherscan shows WETH. The steps that keep a bridge from becoming a wrong wrap are in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains).
description: Circle USDC on Polygon converts to WETH on Ethereum. Buy 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. WETH is not gas. Check Etherscan and keep ETH on chain 1.

sections.heading: WETH cannot start the next Ethereum transaction
sections.body: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is the wrapper. ETH is the gas coin. If the point of this hop was to fund gas on chain id 1, this route is wrong. Choose native ETH instead, then wrap only if a contract demands WETH.

sections.heading: Do not approve USDC.e by habit
sections.body: Wallets often list USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 above native USDC. This quote wants 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. An approval of the bridged contract does not sell the token named here. Read Polygonscan.

sections.heading: POL for the send, ETH for anything after
sections.body: Chain id 137 takes POL. About 2 second blocks there are not the bridge clock. After WETH lands you still need a separate ETH balance on Ethereum, where blocks are about 12 seconds. This quote supplies neither the leftover POL nor that ETH.

sections.heading: Price exposure is real
sections.body: USDC is Circle's dollar token. WETH tracks ether, not a dollar. The minimum on the quote is the floor. Refresh when it expires. If you needed DAI or Tether on Ethereum, you picked the wrong output.

faqs.question: ETH and WETH are the same balance, right?
faqs.answer: No. ETH is native gas. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route delivers the wrapper only. Etherscan can show WETH in the token list while the ETH line stays too low to send it. Keep ETH on chain id 1 if you must move the WETH. The wrapper cannot pay its own transfer.

faqs.question: Which USDC does Polygonscan need to show?
faqs.answer: 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, native Circle USDC on chain id 137. USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is the wrong source. POL pays the fee. The destination contract is checked on Etherscan, not on Polygonscan. POL is only the source fee. Match the native contract on Polygonscan, not the bridged copy.

faqs.question: What if I only needed spendable gas on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Then skip this page. WETH does not pay gas. The native label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the ETH route. Buying the wrapper and then unwrapping costs another transaction you may be unable to send without ETH already there. Fund ETH first or pick native ETH. Do that before you approve.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to USDC on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. Circle USDC is what can arrive on Ethereum. The dollar peg is the easy part. The contract and the issuer are the part people get wrong.

Spend 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, Tether on chain id 137. Receive 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Circle USDC on chain id 1. That is not a bridged USDC copy. Polygonscan shows the Tether debit. Etherscan shows Circle. POL is the source gas. More chain context sits on [Polygon](/chains/polygon).
description: Tether USDT leaves Polygon and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum. Match 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F and 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48.

sections.heading: Ethereum USDT is a different contract
sections.body: If the goal was to keep Tether, Ethereum's contract is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This route buys Circle instead. Deposit instructions that say USDT on Ethereum will not be satisfied by 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48.

sections.heading: Both dollars here use 6 decimals
sections.body: Polygon USDT and Ethereum USDC are 6 decimal tokens, unlike 18 decimal copies on BNB Chain. Still compare the amount on the quote, not a raw log, and still match the full contract. A similar integer does not mean you skipped the issuer change.

sections.heading: USDC on Ethereum is not gas
sections.body: Circle's token will not pay chain id 1. You need ETH there, and blocks are about 12 seconds. That is the chain, not the bridge finish. POL must remain on Polygon, chain id 137, for the send itself.

sections.heading: The source is Polygon Tether only
sections.body: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F does not exist as your balance on Ethereum. Approving Ethereum USDT does nothing for this quote. Confirm chain id 137 in the wallet before the allowance.

faqs.question: Is the arriving USDC the bridged kind?
faqs.answer: No. The credit is native Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. A bridged lookalike is the wrong asset for this quote. Etherscan is the check. If a form asked for USDC.e on another chain, you are in the wrong flow. This credit is native Circle USDC on chain id 1.

faqs.question: Why does Etherscan not show my Polygon USDT?
faqs.answer: Because 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F stays on Polygon. Polygonscan shows it leaving chain id 137. Etherscan shows Circle USDC arriving on chain id 1. They are different ledgers. POL paid the source fee. ETH is required later if you move the USDC. The two explorers never share one balance.

faqs.question: Can I receive Tether if I change my mind on the confirm screen?
faqs.answer: No. The output is fixed by the quote as 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Wanting 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 means a different route. Refresh the quote if the price has moved. There is no finish time printed for the bridge leg. Changing your mind means a new quote, not an edit. The signed quote is the trade.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to DAI on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. Two different issuers, and neither one is Circle.

The debit contract is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. The credit contract is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Polygonscan is the source explorer. Etherscan is the DAI explorer. Chain id 137 uses POL. Chain id 1 uses ETH, with blocks around 12 seconds. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the network that will hold the Maker token.
description: Tether USDT on Polygon converts to Maker DAI on Ethereum. Source 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Confirm DAI on Etherscan, not Polygonscan.

sections.heading: Keeping Tether means a different address
sections.body: Ethereum USDT is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This page never buys it. If an exchange deposit says Tether on Ethereum, stop. DAI from Maker is not a substitute just because both aim near one dollar.

sections.heading: DAI can leave the peg
sections.body: Maker's token at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is not a Circle IOU and not a Tether IOU. The minimum on the quote already includes the market, not a promise of one DAI per one USDT. If that floor is too low, do not sign.

sections.heading: Gas is a third asset
sections.body: POL leaves your Polygon wallet as a fee, not as the thing you are selling. ETH must already sit on Ethereum if you intend to transfer the DAI. Neither stablecoin pays those fees. The 0xEeee label is native gas, and this quote uses it on neither side as the traded asset.

sections.heading: Wrong chain, wasted approval
sections.body: Approving 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Ethereum, or approving Ethereum USDT on Polygon, misses this route. The wallet has to be on chain id 137. Polygonscan should show that exact contract.

faqs.question: Is DAI issued by Tether?
faqs.answer: No. DAI is Maker's token at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. The token you sell is Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygon. Circle is not on either side of this quote. Confirm DAI on Etherscan before you treat it as USDT. The sell side is Tether, and the buy side is Maker. Maker and Circle are different issuers.

faqs.question: What pays the Ethereum transaction after DAI arrives?
faqs.answer: ETH on chain id 1. DAI cannot. Blocks there are about 12 seconds, and that figure is not a bridge finish. This route does not include the ETH. If you have no ETH on Ethereum, the DAI can arrive and wait. Polygon still charges POL for the send.

faqs.question: I wanted Circle USDC on Ethereum. Does DAI count?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC there is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This output is Maker DAI. Using DAI where a form demands USDC is the wrong route. Go back and choose the USDC output before any signature. DAI will not satisfy a Circle deposit. Maker is not a stand-in for Circle on that form.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to ETH on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. Native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. A stable balance becomes the gas coin on chain id 1.

Sell 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Buy the native label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means ETH on Ethereum and not WETH. WETH remains 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 if you needed the wrapper. Polygonscan shows Tether leaving. Etherscan shows ETH. Read [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) if the gas label looks like a token contract.
description: Tether USDT leaves Polygon and native ETH arrives on Ethereum. ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That credit belongs on Etherscan, not WETH.

sections.heading: The label is not a contract to approve
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE has no token bytecode. On chain id 1 it means ETH you can spend on gas. If the wallet asks you to approve that string, you are off this route. Etherscan should show a native credit.

sections.heading: WETH is the wrong finish
sections.body: Contracts that demand 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 will not accept native ETH until you wrap it. Wrapping needs a little extra ETH for gas. If you wanted the wrapper delivered directly, this page is the wrong quote.

sections.heading: Tether on Polygon is not Tether on Ethereum
sections.body: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F is the Polygon contract. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, and this route does not buy it. You are leaving Tether entirely and taking ETH price exposure.

sections.heading: Keep POL for chain 137
sections.body: The source fee is POL, with blocks around 2 seconds. That timing is not the bridge. Ethereum's own blocks are around 12 seconds. Leave POL so the approval of USDT and the swap can both land.

faqs.question: Does 0xEeee mean ETH on Polygon too?
faqs.answer: On Polygon the same label means POL, the gas coin of chain id 137. On Ethereum it means ETH. This route sells Tether, not POL, and it buys Ethereum ETH. Polygonscan will not show the ETH credit. Etherscan will not show the Polygon USDT debit. Polygonscan will not show the ETH credit.

faqs.question: Will I receive WETH if the pool prefers it?
faqs.answer: Not from this quote. The output is native ETH. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, a separate route. ETH is not WETH. If you sign here, plan on a native balance you can later wrap yourself, which takes more ETH for gas. This quote will not deliver the wrapper.

faqs.question: What if the quote shows a weak minimum?
faqs.answer: Do not sign it. USDT against ETH can move before the wallet opens. Request a new quote and read the new floor. No finish time is given for the bridge. About 12 seconds is only Ethereum's block, visible later on Etherscan. Refresh the quote if the floor looks wrong.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to WETH on Ethereum. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. WETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. You take ether price exposure in a wrapper that still cannot pay gas.

The source is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. The destination is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH would be 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and this quote skips it. Polygonscan for the debit, Etherscan for WETH. Chain details for the source are on [Polygon](/chains/polygon).
description: Polygon Tether converts to Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. WETH is not the gas coin. Match it on Etherscan. ETH is separate.

sections.heading: You can arrive unable to move the WETH
sections.body: WETH is not ETH. A fresh Ethereum wallet with only 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 cannot pay the fee to unwrap or transfer it. If funding gas was the goal, this route is wrong. Buy native ETH instead.

sections.heading: Polygon WETH is not this destination
sections.body: Bridged WETH on Polygon is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. You are not selling that. You are selling Tether. If the balance you meant to use is Polygon WETH, stop and open the WETH route.

sections.heading: Tether does not survive the hop
sections.body: Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is a different choice. Maker DAI is another. This page sells the peg and buys wrapped ether. Read the output symbol before you approve 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F.

sections.heading: Two clocks, neither is the bridge
sections.body: Polygon blocks are about 2 seconds. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. The bridge leg has no finish time on this page. POL pays the source. If the quote expires while you compare WETH and ETH, refresh it.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap this WETH without any ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 costs ETH gas on chain id 1. This route does not include that ETH. Etherscan can show a WETH balance and a zero ETH line at the same time. Fund ETH first if you need to touch the wrapper. This hop does not include that gas.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the contract at 0xdAC17?
faqs.answer: No. 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is Ethereum Tether. This route spends 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on chain id 137. Polygonscan is the explorer for that debit. Approving the Ethereum contract does not move the Polygon balance. Check chain id 137 before you sign the allowance. Those Tether contracts are on different chains.

faqs.question: What should I do if I needed native ETH for gas?
faqs.answer: Leave this quote if you needed gas. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and WETH will not pay the next fee. ETH is not WETH. Sign the native output when the funds you move have to pay chain id 1. Etherscan should show ETH, not only the wrapper.

intro:
Swap WETH from Polygon to USDC on Ethereum. Bridged WETH leaves Polygon. Circle USDC is what can arrive on Ethereum. Unwrapping on Polygon is a different job and does not create this USDC.

The token sold is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. The token bought is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Gas on chain id 137 is POL, not this WETH. Gas on chain id 1 is ETH, not this USDC. Polygonscan shows the WETH debit. Etherscan shows Circle. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the distinction between a local unwrap and a real hop.
description: Polygon WETH converts to Circle USDC on Ethereum. Sell 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Confirm the USDC credit on Etherscan. Chain id 1 needs ETH.

sections.heading: Polygon WETH is not Ethereum WETH
sections.body: 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is the Polygon token. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and this quote does not buy it. ETH is not WETH. If you wanted the wrapper to remain a wrapper on mainnet, this USDC route is wrong.

sections.heading: POL pays, even while you sell WETH
sections.body: Chain id 137 will not take WETH as the fee. Leave POL, the native coin behind the label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Blocks are about 2 seconds. That is not a finish time for the bridge. An approval of WETH can be a separate transaction from the swap.

sections.heading: USDC on Ethereum still needs ETH later
sections.body: 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 cannot pay chain id 1. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. If the receiving wallet has no ETH, the USDC can sit there. This route does not attach an ETH stipend.

sections.heading: USDC.e thinking will mislead you
sections.body: The destination is native Circle USDC on Ethereum, not a bridged nickname. Polygon's own USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is irrelevant to this sell. You are selling WETH. If the wallet holds USDC and no WETH, stop.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap this WETH on Polygon and call it Ethereum ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping or selling on Polygon stays on chain id 137, where the gas coin is POL. Ethereum ETH is a different ledger. This route sells 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and can credit Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Etherscan is the credit. Polygonscan is only the debit. Match both contracts before you sign.

faqs.question: Does the USDC pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC is not ETH, and ETH is not WETH. You need ETH already on chain id 1 to move 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 after it arrives. About 12 second blocks describe Ethereum, not the bridge. Keep that ETH separate from the trade. Fund that ETH before you need to move the USDC.

faqs.question: What if I hold POL and think it is WETH?
faqs.answer: POL is native gas, labeled 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and it is not 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. This page cannot spend POL as the principal. If WETH is missing, you are on the wrong route. Use a POL quote instead, and keep some POL for fees. A POL balance is not a WETH balance.

intro:
Swap WETH from Polygon to USDT on Ethereum. Polygon WETH leaves that chain. Tether USDT is what can arrive on Ethereum. You are not delivering Ethereum WETH, and you are not staying in ether.

Sell 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Buy 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, Tether on chain id 1, 6 decimals. Polygonscan records the WETH. Etherscan records Tether. POL is required on the source. The bridge steps that people skip are in [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains).
description: Polygon WETH is sold for Tether USDT on Ethereum. Source 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Read the USDT line on Etherscan. It is not mainnet WETH.

sections.heading: Tether here is the Ethereum contract
sections.body: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not Polygon USDT at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. If you wanted Polygon Tether, you never needed this hop. If you wanted Circle USDC, the contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and this route is wrong.

sections.heading: WETH will not pay Polygon
sections.body: Approving 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 spends a token allowance, and the network fee is still POL. Chain id 137 blocks in about 2 seconds. Leave POL. A wallet that holds only WETH cannot send this route.

sections.heading: USDT will not pay Ethereum
sections.body: After arrival you hold Tether, not ETH. Chain id 1 charges ETH, with blocks around 12 seconds. That block is not the bridge clock. Fund ETH on the destination or the USDT waits. ETH is not WETH, and this output is neither.

sections.heading: Local unwrap is the wrong mental model
sections.body: There is no native ETH inside Polygon to unwrap into. Selling WETH for USDT on Ethereum is a cross-chain trade. Etherscan will not show the Polygon WETH contract as the credit. Match both full addresses.

faqs.question: Is 0xdAC17 the token I am selling?
faqs.answer: No. You sell Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is the Tether you can receive on Ethereum. Polygonscan shows the first. Etherscan shows the second. Approving Ethereum USDT does not move the WETH. Stay on chain id 137 and approve only the Polygon WETH contract before anything else.

faqs.question: Why is my Ethereum WETH balance unchanged?
faqs.answer: Because this quote does not buy 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. ETH is not WETH, and the output is Tether anyway. If you needed mainnet WETH, stop. The credit to look for on Etherscan is USDT, after POL has paid the Polygon fee. Mainnet WETH is a different contract on a different chain.

faqs.question: What happens if I spend my last POL?
faqs.answer: The approval or the swap on chain id 137 fails before Etherscan has a credit to show. WETH cannot substitute for POL. Keep a remainder of the native coin, the 0xEeee label on Polygon. About 2 second blocks are not a promise about the bridge leg.

intro:
Swap WETH from Polygon to DAI on Ethereum. Polygon WETH leaves Polygon. Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. Ether exposure becomes Maker's dollar token, on a chain that still charges ETH for gas.

Debit 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Credit 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. DAI is not Circle and not Tether. Polygonscan is the WETH record. Etherscan is the DAI record. Chain id 1 blocks in about 12 seconds. See [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) for the network that will hold the Maker token.
description: Polygon WETH converts to Maker DAI on Ethereum. The DAI contract is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm that credit on Etherscan. DAI is Maker.

sections.heading: Maker is the issuer on purpose
sections.body: If the instruction says USDC, you want 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. If it says USDT, you want 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F can trade off a dollar. This route is wrong for those other tickers.

sections.heading: Do not send Ethereum WETH into this
sections.body: Mainnet WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 lives on chain id 1. This page sells the Polygon contract only. A wallet left on Ethereum will approve the wrong network. ETH is not WETH on either chain.

sections.heading: POL in, ETH after
sections.body: Source fees are POL on chain id 137. Destination transfers of DAI need ETH. Neither side of the trade is the gas coin. The native label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not what you buy or sell here.

sections.heading: Quote floor, not a one-for-one story
sections.body: WETH against DAI moves. The minimum on the quote is the amount you accept. Refresh if it expires. No finish time is stated for the bridge. Polygon's 2 second blocks only describe chain id 137.

faqs.question: Is DAI from Circle?
faqs.answer: No. Circle issues USDC. DAI is Maker's token at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum. This route sells Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Etherscan should show Maker's contract, not a USDC balance. If your form says Circle, switch routes. Circle USDC is a different contract, a different issuer, and the wrong credit.

faqs.question: Will Polygonscan show the DAI?
faqs.answer: No. Polygonscan shows WETH leaving chain id 137 and POL spent as gas. Etherscan shows DAI on chain id 1. The explorers do not merge. About 12 second Ethereum blocks are not the bridge clock. You still need ETH later to move the DAI. Keep a little ETH on mainnet.

faqs.question: What if the wallet holds WETH on Ethereum already?
faqs.answer: Then you do not need this route to get a Polygon debit. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This page spends the Polygon token. Signing on the wrong chain id approves an unrelated contract. Stay on 137 until the WETH debit is the one you mean. Check the network badge first.

intro:
Swap WETH from Polygon to ETH on Ethereum. Polygon WETH leaves Polygon. Native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. This is not an unwrap button. Polygon has no native ETH to unwrap.

You sell 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. You buy the gas label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which on chain id 1 means ETH you can spend on fees. It is not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Polygonscan shows the token debit. Etherscan shows native ETH. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) uses POL, not this WETH, to pay the source.
description: Polygon WETH becomes native ETH on Ethereum. Sell 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. The ETH credit is native gas on Etherscan. It pays gas too.

sections.heading: Unwrap locally and you are still on Polygon
sections.body: A Polygon unwrap, if a wrapper even offers one, cannot credit chain id 1. Gas there is POL. This route is the one that can end in Ethereum ETH. If you only wanted a different token on Polygon, do not bridge.

sections.heading: The receive can pay mainnet fees
sections.body: Native ETH from the 0xEeee label can pay later Ethereum transactions. WETH cannot until unwrapped. If a contract demanded 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 specifically, this route is the wrong output. ETH is not WETH.

sections.heading: You still spend POL to leave
sections.body: 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 does not pay chain id 137. Keep POL for the approval and the swap. Blocks around 2 seconds are the source chain only. Ethereum blocks around 12 seconds are not a bridge finish time.

sections.heading: Same nickname, two contracts
sections.body: People see WETH and ETH and assume one coin. The sell is a Polygon ERC-20. The buy is native ether on mainnet. Etherscan will not list the Polygon contract as the balance that increased. Match the wallet that signed.

faqs.question: Is this the same as wrapping on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Wrapping on Ethereum stays on chain id 1 and moves between ETH and 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route starts with Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and can finish as native ETH. Polygonscan and Etherscan are both required. ETH is not WETH. A local wrap on Ethereum mainnet is a separate action.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH on Ethereum before I start?
faqs.answer: You need POL on Polygon to send. The ETH credit is what this route can create, so a prior mainnet balance is not required for the credit to exist. You do need the right address on chain id 1. Etherscan shows that native credit, not a WETH token line.

faqs.question: What if I wanted WETH to stay wrapped on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Then this page is wrong. It pays native ETH via 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The wrapped contract is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and is a different quote. Sign this one only if spendable gas on Ethereum is the point. Choose the wrapped output only when a contract demands WETH instead of gas.

intro:
Swap POL from Polygon to USDC on Ethereum. Native POL leaves Polygon. Circle USDC is what can arrive on Ethereum. You spend the gas coin, so the fee and the principal come from one balance.

The source label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning POL on chain id 137, not an ERC-20. The output is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Polygonscan shows POL leaving. Etherscan shows Circle USDC. You will still need ETH on Ethereum to move that USDC. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the chain that charges that later fee.
description: Native POL leaves Polygon and Circle USDC arrives on Ethereum. The POL label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Check Etherscan for USDC. Not ETH.

sections.heading: Do not drain the POL balance
sections.body: Chain id 137 takes POL for gas, about a 2 second block. Sending every unit leaves the transaction unpaid. Wrapped POL or old WMATIC at 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 is not this quote. If that is what you hold, this route is wrong.

sections.heading: USDC is not a gas top-up
sections.body: 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 will not pay chain id 1. ETH will. Blocks there are about 12 seconds, which is not the bridge finish. If the receiving wallet is new, get ETH from somewhere else before you need to transfer the USDC.

sections.heading: The 0xEeee string is not a contract
sections.body: There is nothing to approve. On Polygon it means POL. On Ethereum the same string would mean ETH, but this route does not buy ETH. It buys Circle USDC. Etherscan should show the USDC contract, not a native ETH credit.

sections.heading: Ticker nostalgia is a trap
sections.body: Guides that still say MATIC mean this native POL on chain id 137. A token named MATIC on Ethereum is not what you are selling. Polygonscan is the debit. If the wallet network is not Polygon, stop.

faqs.question: Is 0xEeee something I approve on Polygonscan?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the native gas label for POL on chain id 137. Polygonscan should show a native debit, not an ERC-20 approval of that string. The USDC you can receive is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Approving a random contract is a different action. Native transfers do not use an allowance.

faqs.question: I hold WMATIC. Will this spend it?
faqs.answer: No. Wrapped POL, still often labeled WMATIC, is 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270. This route spends native POL only. If that wrapper is your balance, you are on the wrong asset. Unwrap, or request a quote that names the wrapped contract, and keep native POL for gas. Native POL is the only principal here.

faqs.question: Does the USDC arrive with ETH for fees?
faqs.answer: No. This quote pays Circle USDC, not ETH. ETH is not WETH, and neither one is included as a spare gas balance. You need ETH already on chain id 1 if you want to move 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Etherscan will show the USDC alone. This hop does not attach spare ETH.

intro:
Swap POL from Polygon to USDT on Ethereum. Native POL leaves Polygon. Tether USDT is what can arrive on Ethereum. The gas coin on chain id 137 becomes Tether on chain id 1.

Spend 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Receive 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. There is no approval of the gas label. Polygonscan shows the POL debit. Etherscan shows Tether. Leave POL for the fee or the send cannot start. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains why the gas coin does not keep its name.
description: Native POL on Polygon converts to Tether USDT on Ethereum. Gas label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Confirm USDT on Etherscan. Not Circle USDC.

sections.heading: Tether, not Circle, is the credit
sections.body: Circle USDC on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This page buys 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 instead. A deposit screen that says USDC will reject this Tether. Switch routes before you spend POL.

sections.heading: Wrapped POL is invisible to this quote
sections.body: 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 is the wrapped contract people still call WMATIC. Native POL is the only principal here. Holding the wrapper and an empty native balance means you cannot pay gas and you are selling the wrong asset.

sections.heading: USDT sits until ETH exists
sections.body: Tether cannot pay Ethereum. Chain id 1 blocks take about 12 seconds and that is not the bridge. If you needed spendable ETH, the native output was the right quote. This one pays a 6 decimal stablecoin.

sections.heading: Price moves while POL is volatile
sections.body: You are not moving one dollar to another dollar. POL can reprice against USDT before you sign. Use the minimum on the quote. Polygon blocks near 2 seconds describe only chain id 137.

faqs.question: Will Etherscan show POL?
faqs.answer: No. POL stays a Polygon concept. Etherscan should show Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Polygonscan shows the native debit of 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means POL on chain id 137. The same label on Ethereum would mean ETH, and this route does not buy that. Look for Tether on the destination, not a POL balance.

faqs.question: Can I approve POL like an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: No. The gas label has no contract to approve. If a pop-up asks you to approve 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, you are not on this route. Polygonscan should show a native transfer. Keep a POL remainder so the fee can be paid. There is no allowance on the native gas label.

faqs.question: What if the exchange asked for ERC-20 USDT?
faqs.answer: Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is an ERC-20, so the asset type can match, but the deposit network must say Ethereum. A Polygon deposit address will not see this credit. Etherscan is the check, and you still need ETH to transfer it onward. Match the network name on that deposit page.

intro:
Swap POL from Polygon to DAI on Ethereum. Native POL leaves Polygon. Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. You sell a volatile gas coin for Maker's dollar token.

The source is the native label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The destination is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Polygonscan records POL on chain id 137. Etherscan records DAI on chain id 1. DAI is not Circle USDC and not Tether. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is where that POL balance has to sit before you sign.
description: Native POL leaves Polygon for Maker DAI on Ethereum. DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Match the credit on Etherscan. DAI is not Circle.

sections.heading: Maker DAI can drift
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is not a token Circle redeems and not a Tether IOU. The quote's minimum is the market, not a promise of one dollar of value per unit of POL. If you needed USDC or USDT, this route is wrong.

sections.heading: Leave POL for the network
sections.body: The amount and the fee share one coin. Chain id 137 blocks in about 2 seconds. That speed is not the bridge. WMATIC at 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 will not pay the fee either. Keep native POL.

sections.heading: DAI cannot relay itself
sections.body: On Ethereum you need ETH, with blocks around 12 seconds, to move DAI. This route does not buy the 0xEeee label on Ethereum, so it does not deliver gas. A brand new mainnet wallet will hold DAI and wait.

sections.heading: Do not look for POL on Etherscan
sections.body: The credit is DAI. A token that uses the letters POL on Ethereum is a different asset. Polygonscan is the only explorer for the debit. Match the signing wallet and the full DAI contract.

faqs.question: Is DAI safe to treat as USDC?
faqs.answer: No. USDC is Circle, at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. DAI is Maker at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. This route sells native POL and buys Maker. If a deposit form says Circle, you are on the wrong output. Etherscan shows which contract arrived. Do not send Maker DAI into a Circle-only deposit.

faqs.question: What does the shared gas label mean on this route?
faqs.answer: Only the source uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and on Polygon that is POL. The destination address is the DAI contract, not the gas label. You do not approve POL. Polygonscan shows a native debit. You still must not spend the last POL. A native debit is not an ERC-20 approval.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH before the DAI shows up?
faqs.answer: You need POL to send. You need ETH later if you want to transfer the DAI, because Maker's token is not gas. The route does not include that ETH. About 12 seconds is Ethereum's block on Etherscan, not a finish time for the bridge. Bring ETH on chain id 1 separately.

intro:
Swap POL from Polygon to ETH on Ethereum. Native POL leaves Polygon. Native ETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. Both quotes use the gas label, and they are still two different coins.

0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL on chain id 137 and ETH on chain id 1. There is no ERC-20 on either side of this pair. Polygonscan shows the POL debit. Etherscan shows the ETH credit. Blocks are about 2 seconds on Polygon and about 12 seconds on Ethereum. Neither is the bridge clock. Read [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) before you treat the identical string as one asset.
description: Native POL leaves Polygon and native ETH arrives on Ethereum. Both use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Check Polygonscan, then Etherscan. Not WETH.

sections.heading: Identical text, different coins
sections.body: The gas label is a stand-in, not a shared contract. Spending it on Polygon reduces POL. Receiving it on Ethereum increases ETH. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is not the credit. ETH is not WETH. If you needed the wrapper, switch quotes.

sections.heading: Keep a POL remainder
sections.body: You are spending the fee coin. The last POL cannot pay chain id 137. Wrapped POL at 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 is the wrong balance. This route never approves that contract.

sections.heading: The ETH you receive can pay mainnet
sections.body: That is the point of buying the native label on chain id 1. It is not a stablecoin. POL against ETH can move before you sign. Take the minimum or refresh the quote. No finish time is published here.

sections.heading: X-chain confusion is a different network
sections.body: This hop is Polygon to Ethereum, not Avalanche. Etherscan is the destination explorer. If someone told you to watch Snowtrace, they described a different route. Stay with chain id 1 for the credit.

faqs.question: Why do both addresses match?
faqs.answer: Because 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE marks native gas on each EVM chain. On Polygon, chain id 137, it is POL. On Ethereum, chain id 1, it is ETH. You do not approve it. Polygonscan shows the debit and Etherscan shows the credit. They are not one balance. Do not approve that label.

faqs.question: Is this a way to turn POL into WETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route pays native ETH. ETH is not WETH. If a contract call needs the wrapper, wrap after the ETH arrives, which spends a little of that ETH on gas. Etherscan should show a native balance first. ETH is not WETH at any point here.

faqs.question: What if I hold WMATIC instead of POL?
faqs.answer: Then stop. The wrapped contract is 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270. This page spends native POL only. You also need native POL for the fee, so a wallet of only the wrapper cannot complete chain id 137. Unwrap, then leave a remainder. The wrapper and the native coin are different lines.

intro:
Swap POL from Polygon to WETH on Ethereum. Native POL leaves Polygon. WETH is what can arrive on Ethereum. The wrapper you receive cannot pay gas, so this is a poor way to fund a new Ethereum wallet.

Sell the POL label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Buy 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH would use that same gas label on chain id 1, and this quote refuses it. Polygonscan shows POL. Etherscan shows WETH. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where you will need a separate ETH balance afterward.
description: Native POL on Polygon converts to WETH on Ethereum. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and cannot pay gas. Check Etherscan. Native ETH differs.

sections.heading: WETH at the end strands a gas-poor wallet
sections.body: If the job was to pay Ethereum fees, this route is wrong. 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 does not pay them. Native ETH does. ETH is not WETH. Pick the native output when the next transaction has to be funded by what arrives.

sections.heading: POL is not the wrapped contract
sections.body: 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 is wrapped POL or legacy WMATIC. This quote spends native POL and still needs some of it left for chain id 137. Blocks there are about 2 seconds and are not the bridge finish.

sections.heading: Do not expect Ethereum WETH to be the thing you held
sections.body: You did not hold 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 before this trade unless you already used Ethereum. The credit is new. The debit is POL. Etherscan and Polygonscan will not show one transfer.

sections.heading: Volatile in, volatile wrapper out
sections.body: POL and ether both move. The minimum on the quote is your floor. Refresh when it stales. A stablecoin output is the right page when you wanted dollars instead of WETH.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap the received WETH with no ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 costs ETH on chain id 1. This route does not deliver that ETH. Etherscan can list WETH while the ETH line is empty. If you needed gas, buy native ETH via 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE instead. WETH cannot pay the unwrap if the ETH line is empty.

faqs.question: Does Polygonscan approve the gas label?
faqs.answer: It should not. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native POL on chain id 137, not a contract. You should see a native debit. If you are approving WMATIC at 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270, you are on the wrong token for this page. Native POL and that wrapped contract are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: What if I wanted USDC rather than price exposure?
faqs.answer: Leave this quote. Circle USDC on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. WETH tracks ether, not a dollar. You would still need ETH later to move the USDC. Read the output before you spend POL. Switch to a Circle USDC quote if you want dollars on Ethereum instead of WETH.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to USDT on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. Tether USDT is what can arrive on BNB Chain. The issuer changes, and the destination token uses 18 decimals.

Sell 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, native USDC on chain id 137, 6 decimals. Buy 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, Tether on chain id 56, 18 decimals. Polygonscan shows the debit. BscScan shows the credit. POL pays the source. BNB pays anything you do later on BNB Chain. The destination network is [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc).
description: Circle USDC leaves Polygon and 18 decimal Tether arrives on BNB Chain. Spend 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Confirm it on BscScan. Decimals differ.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals will scare a raw-log reader
sections.body: Polygon USDC is 6 decimals. BNB Chain USDT is 18. The quote speaks in human units. Comparing integers across Polygonscan and BscScan invents a missing balance. Read the amount on the quote, then the contract.

sections.heading: USDC.e is the wrong Polygon dollar
sections.body: 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 will not fill this quote. Native Circle USDC is the named source. If the wallet lists the bridged copy first, you are one tap from the wrong approval.

sections.heading: Keeping Circle means a different BNB Chain contract
sections.body: Circle USDC on BNB Chain is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, also 18 decimals. This route buys Tether instead. If the deposit must stay Circle, this page is wrong.

sections.heading: Two gas coins, neither is the trade
sections.body: Leave POL on chain id 137, about 2 second blocks. Leave BNB on chain id 56, about 3 second blocks, if you need to move the USDT after it arrives. Neither block time is the bridge finish. USDT will not pay BNB Chain fees.

faqs.question: Is BNB Chain USDT the same as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and uses 6 decimals. This credit is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on chain id 56 and uses 18 decimals. BscScan is the explorer. Approving the Ethereum contract does nothing for this hop. Chain id 56 is BNB Chain, and Etherscan will not list this credit.

faqs.question: What if I hold USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. The quote spends 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Polygonscan shows which one you approved. You still need POL on chain id 137 for gas, separate from either dollar token. Approve only native Circle USDC, then confirm that address on Polygonscan. Do it before you sign.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay BNB Chain gas?
faqs.answer: No. Tether is not BNB. BNB is the native coin, labeled 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. This route does not buy that label. Keep BNB in the destination wallet or the new USDT cannot be moved. BscScan will show the token without showing a gas credit.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to ETH on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. Binance-Peg ETH is what can arrive on BNB Chain. That token is not native ether and it will not pay BNB Chain fees.

Sell 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Buy 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and is not involved. Polygonscan shows the USDC. BscScan shows the peg. Chain id 56 charges BNB, with blocks around 3 seconds. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is useful if the ticker ETH still looks like mainnet gas.
description: Circle USDC on Polygon becomes Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. It does not pay gas. Check BscScan.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH cannot pay chain 56
sections.body: 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is a BEP-20. Gas is BNB, the native label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. If you needed BNB to move tokens afterward, this route is wrong. A wallet with only the peg sits still.

sections.heading: USDC.e is not the source
sections.body: The bridged dollar 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is a different Polygon balance. This quote spends native Circle USDC. Polygonscan shows the approval target. Chain id 137 must be selected, and POL must remain for the fee.

sections.heading: Mainnet ether is chain id 1
sections.body: Etherscan and about 12 second blocks belong to Ethereum. This credit is on BNB Chain. ETH is not WETH, and this peg is a third asset. If your ether is on Ethereum, you are on the wrong network for this page.

sections.heading: Decimals and the peg
sections.body: Polygon USDC uses 6 decimals. The pegged token uses 18. Read the human amount on the quote. BscScan will not show a native BNB credit for this pair. POL on the source, about 2 second blocks, is not the bridge clock.

faqs.question: Is Binance-Peg ETH the same as WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on chain id 1. This route buys 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on chain id 56. ETH is not WETH, and the peg is neither of them. BscScan is the explorer for the credit. Etherscan will not list this debit. Do not treat the peg as mainnet gas.

faqs.question: Will this fund gas on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: No. The peg cannot pay fees. BNB does, and this quote does not buy the native label. Keep BNB in the destination wallet or the new token cannot move. Blocks near 3 seconds describe BNB Chain only, not the bridge finish. Fund BNB before you need to move the peg.

faqs.question: What if my USDC is the bridged Polygon kind?
faqs.answer: Then stop. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This page spends 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Polygonscan will show an approval of the wrong contract if you force the bridged token. POL is still required on chain id 137. Switch to native Circle USDC before you approve, or the bridged balance stays put.

intro:
Swap USDC from Polygon to BNB on BNB Chain. Circle USDC leaves Polygon. Native BNB is what can arrive on BNB Chain. You sell a dollar token and receive the coin that pays fees on chain id 56.

The source is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. The destination is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the native gas label, meaning BNB here and not WBNB. Polygonscan shows USDC leaving. BscScan shows BNB. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is chain id 56, with blocks around 3 seconds.
description: Circle USDC leaves Polygon and native BNB arrives on chain id 56. The BNB label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Confirm it on BscScan. Not WBNB.

sections.heading: The label is not WBNB
sections.body: WBNB is 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. This quote does not buy it. If a pool asked for the wrapped contract, this route is wrong. Native BNB can pay later fees. There is nothing to approve on the destination side of that label.

sections.heading: Do not start from USDC.e
sections.body: Native Circle USDC is the named sell. The older bridged token is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. Approving that contract spends the wrong balance. Match 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan.

sections.heading: POL in, BNB out
sections.body: Chain id 137 still charges POL, about 2 second blocks. That POL does not become the BNB you receive. Leave enough POL for the USDC approval and the swap. Draining POL fails the send before BscScan shows a credit.

sections.heading: The peg ends
sections.body: USDC is Circle's dollar token. BNB moves with its own market. Accept the minimum or refresh the quote. No finish time is given for the bridge. A stablecoin output on BNB Chain is a different page.

faqs.question: Do I approve 0xEeee on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the native gas label for BNB on chain id 56. BscScan should show a native credit, not an ERC-20 approval. The token you sell is Circle USDC on Polygon. If a wallet asks you to approve the gas label, you are off this route.

faqs.question: Is WBNB what arrives?
faqs.answer: No. WBNB lives at 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c. This page pays native BNB, which can pay gas. If you needed the wrapper for a contract, wrap after arrival or pick a quote that names WBNB. ETH is not WETH, and BNB is not WBNB. Wrap only after native BNB is already in the wallet.

faqs.question: Can USDC.e take this path?
faqs.answer: Not this quote. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. You need 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 plus POL on chain id 137. Polygonscan shows which contract was approved. The BNB credit is only on BscScan. The bridged USDC.e balance will not sell on this page. Use only the native Circle contract. Check the approval on Polygonscan.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to USDC on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. Circle USDC is what can arrive on BNB Chain. You change issuer, and you also change decimals from 6 to 18.

Spend 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Circle USDC on chain id 56. That is not Tether's 18 decimal token at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. Polygonscan, then BscScan. POL pays the source. BNB is required later if you move the USDC. See [how to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains).
description: Polygon Tether converts to Circle USDC on BNB Chain. The USDC contract is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d and uses 18 decimals. Check BscScan.

sections.heading: Staying in Tether is a different contract
sections.body: 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is BNB Chain USDT. This route buys Circle instead. Deposit instructions that say USDT will not be met by 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Stop if the ticker has to stay Tether.

sections.heading: The raw integer jumps
sections.body: Six decimals become eighteen. The quote already converts human amounts. A huge integer on BscScan is not a windfall, and a small one on Polygonscan is not a loss. Read the decimal amount, then the contract.

sections.heading: USDC still needs BNB
sections.body: Circle's token on chain id 56 does not pay gas. BNB does. Blocks there are about 3 seconds and are not the bridge finish. A destination wallet with no BNB can hold USDC and fail the next transfer.

sections.heading: Polygon Tether is not Ethereum Tether
sections.body: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is the Ethereum contract. This page spends 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on chain id 137. Leave POL for that chain. An approval on the wrong network does nothing.

faqs.question: Is BNB Chain USDC 6 decimals like Polygon USDT?
faqs.answer: No. 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d uses 18 decimals. Polygon Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F uses 6. Compare the amount on the quote. BscScan shows the Circle contract. Polygonscan shows the Tether debit. The integers will not match. A larger raw integer is only the decimals gap, not a larger payment.

faqs.question: What if I needed USDT on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. Tether there is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. You would be buying Circle at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Issuers are not interchangeable on a deposit form. Switch the output before you approve anything on Polygon. Tether on BNB Chain is a separate route with its own 18 decimal contract.

faqs.question: Does the USDC pay the next BNB Chain fee?
faqs.answer: No. You need native BNB, the gas label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 56. This quote does not buy it. About 3 second blocks are the chain, not the bridge. Keep BNB in the receiving wallet if you must move the USDC. USDC is not a substitute for that gas coin.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to ETH on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. Binance-Peg ETH is what can arrive on BNB Chain. The word ETH here is a BEP-20, not gas, and not Ethereum WETH.

Sell 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Buy 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Native BNB is a different line. Polygonscan shows Tether. BscScan shows the peg. Chain id 56 blocks in about 3 seconds. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is only the network you sign on.
description: Polygon Tether converts to Binance-Peg ETH, 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. That token is not BNB and not WETH. Confirm the peg on BscScan.

sections.heading: Three assets people call ETH
sections.body: Native ETH pays Ethereum. WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route buys neither. It buys the BNB Chain peg. If your balance is on chain id 1, Etherscan is the wrong explorer and this page is the wrong route.

sections.heading: The peg will not start the next transaction
sections.body: BNB pays chain id 56. If the goal was gas, buy the native label instead. Arriving with only 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 leaves you unable to move it. That is the wrong output for a gas top-up.

sections.heading: Tether does not come along
sections.body: BNB Chain USDT is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. This quote does not buy it. You leave the dollar peg and take pegged-ETH price exposure. Read the output before you approve 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F.

sections.heading: POL remains the source fee
sections.body: Chain id 137 charges POL, about 2 second blocks. Those blocks are not the bridge. Leave POL. The destination fee, if you move the peg later, is BNB and is not included.

faqs.question: Does BscScan treat this peg as Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The contract 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 can be named like Ethereum and still be a BEP-20 on chain id 56. It is not native ETH and not WETH. BNB is the only gas coin there. Read the contract on BscScan, not the ticker alone. The name can say Ethereum and still be the peg.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the same as BNB Chain USDT?
faqs.answer: No. You sell 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. BNB Chain Tether is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, and this route does not buy it. Polygonscan shows the debit. If you wanted to keep Tether, choose that output instead of the peg. Keeping a dollar peg means Tether or Circle, not this output. Pick one before you sign.

faqs.question: What pays fees after the peg arrives?
faqs.answer: BNB, not the peg and not POL. The native label on chain id 56 is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. This quote does not buy it. About 3 second blocks are not a bridge finish time. Fund BNB separately if you need to transfer the peg. The peg itself never becomes gas.

intro:
Swap USDT from Polygon to BNB on BNB Chain. Tether USDT leaves Polygon. Native BNB is what can arrive on BNB Chain. A 6 decimal stablecoin becomes the gas coin on chain id 56.

You sell 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. You buy 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means BNB on this destination, not WBNB. Polygonscan shows the Tether debit. BscScan shows native BNB. There is no approval of the gas label. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers why that label changes meaning with the chain.
description: Tether USDT on Polygon converts to native BNB on chain id 56. BNB is the gas label 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Check BscScan, not an approval.

sections.heading: WBNB is the wrong finish
sections.body: 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c is the wrapped contract. This page pays native BNB, which can pay fees. If a router demanded WBNB, wrap afterward or change the quote. Signing here and expecting the wrapper is the wrong route.

sections.heading: You leave Tether on purpose
sections.body: Keeping dollars on BNB Chain would mean USDT at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 or Circle USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Both are 18 decimals. This route buys BNB instead. Price can move.

sections.heading: POL must survive the send
sections.body: The source fee is POL on chain id 137. Tether cannot pay it. About 2 second Polygon blocks are not the bridge clock. Leave POL even though the thing you want on the other side is a gas coin.

sections.heading: No bytecode behind the receive address

faqs.question: Is the arriving BNB an ERC-20 I must approve?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is native BNB on chain id 56. There is no approval. BscScan shows a native credit. WBNB at 0xbb4CdB9CBd36B01bD1cBaEBF2De08d9173bc095c is a different asset. The token you sold is Polygon Tether, visible on Polygonscan. Do not approve the gas label. WBNB is a later wrap if a pool demands it.

faqs.question: Will my Tether balance on BNB Chain increase?
