sections.heading: Native POL has to survive the Solana hop
sections.body: The native label is both the asset and the fee. Wrapped POL will not pay chain id 137. Drain native POL and the send fails. About 2 second blocks are not the bridge.

sections.heading: USDT waits without SOL
sections.body: This route does not buy So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. A Phantom wallet with no SOL can hold the mint and fail the next transfer.

sections.heading: Not an EVM receive
sections.body: Do not paste a 0x address. Phantom and Solscan are the destination. There is no chain id and no allowance on the mint.

faqs.question: Will Solscan show POL?
faqs.answer: No. POL stays on Polygon. Solscan should show Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Polygonscan shows the native debit of 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means POL on chain id 137. There is no ERC-20 approval of that label. The same label is not a Solana mint. Look up the Tether mint on Solscan, not a POL balance.

faqs.question: Can I approve POL?
faqs.answer: No. The gas label is not a contract. If the wallet asks you to approve 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, stop. You should see a native debit on Polygonscan. Keep a remainder so the fee can be paid. The receiver is a Phantom address, not 0x. Solana never asks for an ERC-20 allowance on that mint.

faqs.question: Is this the Circle mint?
faqs.answer: No. Circle on Solana is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. This credit is Tether. Issuers are not interchangeable on a deposit form. You still need SOL later, because USDT is not the fee coin. There is no finish time for the bridge. Bring SOL if you need to move the Tether after it arrives.

intro:
Swap POL from Polygon to SOL on Solana. Native POL leaves Polygon. SOL is what can arrive on Solana. You trade one network's gas coin for the other's, across two account models.

POL is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 137. SOL is quoted as So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Those strings are not the same kind of address. Polygonscan shows the POL debit. Solscan shows SOL. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. [Solana](/chains/solana) is where the credit can pay later fees.
description: Native POL leaves Polygon and SOL arrives on Solana. The gas label is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Confirm SOL on Solscan. Phantom. Not ERC-20.

sections.heading: Leave a POL remainder
sections.body: You are spending the fee coin. The last POL cannot pay chain id 137. Wrapped POL at 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 is the wrong balance. This quote wants native POL only.

sections.heading: Phantom's name for this SOL credit
sections.body: Phantom spends that balance as SOL. It is not an ERC-20, not WETH, and not WBTC. WBTC is not native bitcoin, and this hop does not involve bitcoin. Solscan is the check.

sections.heading: POL and SOL do not share a peg
sections.body: POL and SOL are volatile against each other. The minimum on the quote is the deal. Refresh it if you pause. Nothing here dates the bridge. A 2 second Polygon block only means the source chain moved.

sections.heading: Circle and Tether are other Solana quotes
sections.body: Circle USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Tether is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. If you needed either peg, this SOL route is wrong.

faqs.question: Are the two gas labels the same address type?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is an EVM stand-in for POL on chain id 137. So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is a Solana mint for SOL. You do not approve either one as an ERC-20 on Solana. Polygonscan and Solscan are separate records. A 0x string is not a Solana receiver. Check Solscan with the Phantom address you pasted.

faqs.question: Can I receive SOL in the Polygon wallet?
faqs.answer: Only if that wallet also has a Solana address, such as Phantom, and you pasted that address. The 0x account on chain id 137 is not a Solana receiver. There is no ERC-20 approval that fixes a wrong address type. Solscan shows the mint after the hop.

faqs.question: What if the wallet holds wrapped POL?
faqs.answer: Then this route cannot spend it. The wrapper is 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270. Native POL is the gas label. Unwrap, or request a quote that names the wrapper. You still must keep native POL for the chain id 137 fee. Unwrap first. A wrapper-only balance cannot pay chain id 137.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to USDT on Ethereum. Native Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One. Tether USDT is what can arrive on Ethereum. You change issuer on the way from a layer 2 to mainnet, and USDC.e is the wrong token to start from.

Sell 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on chain id 42161, not Nova and not USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. Buy 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on chain id 1. Arbiscan shows the debit. Etherscan shows Tether. ETH pays gas on both chains, and the balances are separate. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is not Ethereum, even though both use ETH.
description: Native USDC on Arbitrum One becomes Tether on Ethereum. Check Arbiscan, then Etherscan. This is not USDC.e and not Circle on mainnet. Chain ids 42161 and 1.

sections.heading: USDC.e is the wrong start
sections.body: If the wallet holds 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8, this quote cannot spend it. Native USDC is the named token. Arbiscan shows which contract you approved. Nova is the wrong network.

sections.heading: Keeping Circle means a different mainnet contract
sections.body: Ethereum USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This page buys Tether instead. A deposit that says Circle USDC on Ethereum will not accept 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7.

sections.heading: ETH on both sides, still two balances
sections.body: You need ETH on Arbitrum One to send and ETH on Ethereum to move the USDT after it arrives. USDT is not gas. About 12 second blocks are Ethereum, not a bridge finish time. The ARB token does not pay either side.

sections.heading: Not a same-asset canonical bridge
sections.body: A hop that keeps Circle USDC would be a different route. This one changes issuer while it changes chain. If your only goal was the same coin on mainnet, stop and pick USDC.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum USDC.e valid here?
faqs.answer: No. USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. This route spends native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. The credit is Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Arbiscan and Etherscan are separate. The ticker USDC is not enough. Nova is the wrong network, and USDC.e is the wrong token.

faqs.question: Will the USDT pay Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not ETH. Chain id 1 charges ETH, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. That block time is not a finish time for the bridge. Keep ETH on Ethereum or the new USDT cannot move. ETH on Arbitrum does not cover mainnet.

faqs.question: What if I wanted Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Then this route is wrong. Ethereum USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This output is Tether. Circle and Tether are different issuers. Switch before you approve the Arbitrum USDC. Etherscan should show the contract you chose. Circle USDC on Ethereum is a different contract. Do not deposit Tether where Circle was requested.

intro:
Swap USDC from Arbitrum One to DAI on Ethereum. Native Circle USDC leaves Arbitrum One. Maker DAI is what can arrive on Ethereum. You switch from Circle to Maker, and you land on mainnet where gas is ETH.

The debit is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, not USDC.e. The credit is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Arbiscan records the USDC on chain id 42161. Etherscan records Maker's DAI on chain id 1. Not Nova. DAI can trade away from one dollar. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that DAI contract lives.
description: Native USDC on Arbitrum One converts to Maker DAI on Ethereum. DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm that credit on Etherscan only.

sections.heading: Maker, not Circle and not Tether
sections.body: If you needed Ethereum USDC, the contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. If you needed Tether, it is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. DAI is neither. This route is wrong for those tickers.

sections.heading: Bridged USDC on Arbitrum will not sell
sections.body: 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is the older bridged dollar on Arbitrum. This page wants native USDC. Approving USDC.e spends a token the quote did not name. Check Arbiscan.

sections.heading: DAI cannot pay mainnet
sections.body: After the credit you still need ETH on chain id 1. DAI is not gas, and ETH is not WETH. About 12 second blocks are Ethereum, not the bridge. This quote does not buy the native ETH label.

sections.heading: ETH on Arbitrum is a separate fee
sections.body: Chain id 42161 charges its own ETH. The ARB token will not pay it. Nova is the wrong network. Leave ETH on Arbitrum One so the send can land.

faqs.question: Is DAI issued by Circle?
faqs.answer: No. USDC is Circle. DAI is Maker's token at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Ethereum. This route sells native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbitrum One, not USDC.e and not Nova. Etherscan should show Maker's contract. If your form says Circle or Tether, switch routes. Maker is not a stand-in for Circle or Tether on a deposit form.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH on both chains?
faqs.answer: You need ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, to send, and ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1, if you want to move the DAI afterward. DAI will not pay mainnet. The route does not include that mainnet ETH. About 12 second blocks are not the bridge clock. Arbiscan and Etherscan do not share a balance.

faqs.question: What if the wallet is on Nova or holds USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Then stop. Nova is not Arbitrum One. USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8, not 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Arbiscan shows the contract you approved. The DAI credit, if you use the right token, appears only on Etherscan. You must start on Arbitrum One with native USDC, or this DAI credit will not be the one you expect.
